summary: Feed s181_triple is degraded for IDS: 28.7% one-way TCP sessions (needs both directions), 3.6 Gbps microbursts overloading 1 Gbps IDS port, and 76.6% encrypted traffic exceeds 60% IDS tolerance.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is delivering only one direction for 45 of 157 TCP sessions (28.7%). Likely asymmetric TAP/SPAN feeds not aggregated or hash-based distribution splitting client->server and server->client across different tool ports.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs both directions to reassemble TCP streams and track state. One-way traffic breaks stream reassembly, causes missed exploit detection and false/incomplete alerts.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate both directions of each bidirectional flow to the same IDS port so the IDS sees complete sessions for stateful inspection.

findings.root_cause: Microbursts peaking at 3.60 Gbps in 1ms intervals hitting a 1 Gbps IDS port (360% of capacity, 2 overloaded intervals). Packet broker is not load-balancing or buffering bursts to match tool capacity.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS ingress buffers overflow and silently drop packets during bursts, creating blind spots exactly during high-volume events when detection is most critical.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute traffic across multiple 1 Gbps IDS ports or add load-balancing to keep per-port rate <80% and prevent burst drops; IDS needs full payload so slicing is not an option.

findings.root_cause: 76.6% of bytes are encrypted vs IDS tolerance of ~60%. Traffic has shifted to TLS/encrypted protocols without a visibility decryption layer before the IDS.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS is blind to payload inside encrypted sessions; signatures, exploit and C2 detection cannot fire, sharply reducing detection coverage.

recommended_fix.why: Add out-of-band SSL/TLS visibility (decryption) or selective decrypt policy before IDS, or route decrypted copy to IDS, to restore payload visibility within tool tolerance.
